claims.text: The equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi baseline and all compared equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets are single-phase FCC after identical thermomechanical processing.
Constituent count alone is inadequate to explain the mechanical-property differences among these alloys.
Local chemical short-range order differs systematically between the quinary alloy and its ternary and quaternary subsets.
Local chemical short-range order alters stacking-fault energy in these CrMnFeCoNi-derived alloys.
Local chemical short-range order alters magnetic configurations in these alloys.
The presence of Mn in CrMnFeCoNi produces magnetic frustration.
Mn-induced magnetic frustration disrupts short-range order favorable for nanotwinning and dislocation interactions.
Reducing or removing Mn in ternary and quaternary subsets produces a more ordered local atomic arrangement.
CrCoNi has a lower stacking-fault energy than the CrMnFeCoNi baseline.
Lower stacking-fault energy in the lower-constituent alloys enhances deformation-twin nucleation.
Reducing or removing Mn facilitates dislocation mobility.
More favorable short-range order can enhance ultimate strength and ductility.
Enhanced nanotwinning and dislocation motion delay strain localization and failure.
CrCoNi has a superior combination of strength and plastic deformation relative to CrMnFeCoNi.
The ternary alloys, and to a lesser extent the quaternary alloys, will have greater ultimate strength and ductility than the quinary baseline.
The ternary and quaternary alloys will develop a higher density of deformation-induced twins than the quinary baseline.
The ternary and quaternary alloys will exhibit less dislocation pile-up than the quinary baseline.
The proposed comparison is restricted to identically processed, initially single-phase FCC samples tested at room temperature and controlled strain rate.
The hypothesis would be falsified if short-range order does not differ systematically across the alloys or if the predicted twin and mechanical-property enhancements are absent.

contradictions.description: The mechanism treats the ternary and quaternary subsets collectively as involving reduction or removal of Mn, but many such subsets retain Mn. In an equiatomic Mn-containing quaternary or ternary subset, Mn is 25 or 33.3 at.%, respectively, rather than the quinary baseline's 20 at.%, so its atomic fraction is increased rather than reduced. The Mn-removal mechanism therefore cannot consistently explain predictions made for all subsets.
